verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew successfully splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "splashing down in the Pacific Ocean Friday evening" "off the coast of San Diego" "Apr 10, 2026" "5:07 p.m. Pacific time" "Splashdown confirmed at 7:07 p.m. Central time, 5:07 p.m. Pacific time."
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm the location, date, time, and successful splashdown in the Pacific off San Diego.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew completed their 10-day mission around the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "capping a nearly 10-day journey around the moon" "nearly 10-day flight" "10-day lunar flyby" "After 10 days circling the Earth, the moon"
verifications.reasoning: Sources consistently describe the mission as approximately or exactly 10 days with a lunar flyby/around the Moon; launch April 1 to splashdown April 10 confirms duration.

verifications.claim: Footage shows the Artemis II capsule's parachute deployment and recovery.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: "From parachute deployment to splashdown, watch the full historic moment in the video above." "And there go the first series of parachutes... 3 good main chutes." "Watch in our video player above."
verifications.reasoning: Sources provide footage explicitly from parachute deployment to splashdown, but do not confirm footage of post-splashdown recovery operations.

verifications.claim: Coverage of the Artemis II capsule's parachute deployment and recovery is available on NASA's YouTube channel.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: "Live mission coverage is available on NASA’s YouTube channel." "You can stream the Artemis II return free on NASA+ at plus.nasa.gov or on NASA's YouTube channel."
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm live return/splashdown coverage on YouTube, which includes parachute deployment per timeline, but not explicitly recovery.

verifications.claim: Coverage of the Artemis II capsule's parachute deployment and recovery is available via AP News.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew's safe return completes the first crewed mission to the Moon in over 50 years.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "first lunar voyage in more than a half-century" "first humans toward the Moon since 1972" "first crewed mission to the moon in more than 50 years"
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm safe/successful return and explicitly describe it as the first crewed lunar mission since 1972 (over 50 years).
